ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AD \parallel BE \parallel CF$, where points $B, E$ are on $AC, DF$ respectively, $\frac{AB}{BC} = \frac{2}{3}, EF = 6$. What is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD\parallel BE\parallel CF$, \\
it follows that $\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{DE}{FE}$, \\
thus $DE=\boxed{4}$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AD \parallel BE \parallel CF$, where points $B, E$ are on $AC, DF$ respectively, $\frac{AB}{BC} = \frac{2}{3}$ and $EF = 6$. What is the length of $DE$?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Since $AD \parallel BE \parallel CF$, it follows that $\frac{AB}{BC} = \frac{DE}{FE}$, thus $DE = 4$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three horizontal straight lines parallel to one another; an oblique line on the left intersects them in order at A, B, C, and another oblique line on the right intersects them in order at D, E, F; therefore AD, BE, CF are respectively located on the three parallel lines, B is on AC, and E is on DF. The problem gives AB/BC = 2/3, EF = 6. Reasoning: Three parallel lines are cut by two oblique transversals; according to the intercept theorem, the corresponding intercepted line segments are proportional, so DE/EF = AB/BC = 2/3. Substituting EF = 6 gives DE = (2/3) × 6 = 4.
